glyph_origin: Phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 禾 (“wheat; grain”) + phonetic 人. Originally meaning "harvest", it later came to mean "year". In the oracle bone script and early bronze inscriptions, it was originally written like 秂. In bronze inscriptions after the Western Zhou period, a stroke was often added to 人 to give 千, which still acted as a phonetic component, thus getting (秊). The current form is inherited from the clerical script, where libian (隸變) has occurred.
